items.html: A fast bowler from Antigua, Kerry Jeremy's early career was blighted by injury. He broke into the West Indies side in the 2000 ICC Champions Trophy, retaining his place on the 2000-01 tour of Australia but he suffered a broken jaw early on and played little part.  He recovered in time to win selection for the 2000-01 tour of Zimbabwe but broke down with a serious back strain and had to return home.  He continued to perform well at domestic level but has, as yet, not been considered again for selection.

images.caption: Kerry Jeremy holds his broken jaw as Dujon accompanies him back
images.longCaption: West Indies tailender Kerry Jeremy (L) holds his jaw as he walks from the WACA ground accompanied by assistant coach Jeffrey Dujon (R) during a four-day game against the Western Warriors (a West Australian state side) at the WACA ground in Perth 09 November 2000. Jeremy was hit in the face by a delivery from Matthew Nicholson and was forced to retire injured on seven runs, with the West Indies innings coming to an end on 9 for 132. He was transferred to hospital to get a cautionary X-ray for his jaw.
